 Melbourne Cup 2026: Point of Law wins Cup, Ciaron Maher trains trifecta Share Share article Melbourne Cup 2026: Point of Law wins Cup, Ciaron Maher trains trifecta
 By Andrew McGarry
 M By Michael Doyle
 Topic: Horse Racing
 Posted Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 9:45am Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 9:45am Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 9:45am , updated Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 5:33pm Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 5:33pm Skip to timeline abc.net.au/news/melbourne-cup-2026-live-flemington/107335812 Link copied Share Share article Point of Law, a horse sold by King Charles III in July, has won the Melbourne Cup in just its sixth start.
 The three-year-old colt trained by Ciaron Maher firmed as the favourite just before the jump, taking the tag away from Hopewell Rock, which began the day as the most fancied to win the famous 3,200m race.
 Loading Twitter content Ridden by Alice Springs native Ethan Brown, Point of Law stormed home late, chasing down long-time leader Royal Supremacy with 150 metres to go, to win ahead of Zahrann and Juja Kibo. 
 Mahar became the first trainer in Melbourne Cup history to train the trifecta.
 Loading Twitter content Point of Law, the son of famous champion Frankle, was bred in England and owned by King Charles III before being sold in August to an Australian consortium following his Group 3 Bahrain Trophy win at Newmarket.
 Its two runs in Australia have both been victorious after winning October's Geelong Cup, becoming just the fourth horse to claim the Geelong-Melbourne Cup double after Media Puzzle (2002), Americain (2010) and Dunaden (2011).
 Earlier, Chris Waller-trained Asterix was scratched from the Cup after stewards deemed medication had been used on the horse today. Waller explained it was a simple mistake in the heat of the moment .
 Look back at all the action of Melbourne Cup Day at Flemington in our live blog below.

 Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 3:19pm Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 3:19pm Ciaron Maher becomes first trainer to trifecta the Melbourne Cup
 M By Michael Doyle
 Loading Twitter content Superstar trainer   Ciaron Maher had seven runners in this year's Melbourne Cup.
 And three of them have managed to finish first, second and third.
 The Maher trifecta — Point of Law,   Zahrann and Juja Kibo — is a phenomenal achievement. He is the first trainer to ever achieve that feat.
 "It's been a whirlwind, really, but I'm very proud of all the team," he tells the Nine broadcast.
 "Like to get three horses in the first three spots. I don't even know where the rest finished yet, but very proud."

 Loading Twitter content Ethan Brown has won the Melbourne Cup, a magical moment for the lad from Alice Springs.
 "Please don't wake me up," he tells the Nine Network.
 He thanks Point of Law's trainer, Ciaron Maher.
 "He took me out of horse training at one stage when I was about 22 years old. But yeah, he's done nothing but support me and backed me and I buggered up plenty of times on his horses and 
he just he's had nothing but faith," he says.
 Speaking of Point of Law, there was plenty of belief in this young horse and it had come through with flying colours.
 "Just stay cool, stay patient, cut the bend. And once he 
got that clear running, his turn of foot was enormous. He's going to be a superstar horse. This horse is something special."

 Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 3:02pm Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 3:02pm We're ready for the Melbourne Cup!
 A By Andrew McGarry
 Here we go, folks!
 The 23 runners are at the barriers for this year's Melbourne Cup, and it won't be long before they're off.
 Who will take the glory this time, and who will make the story in this 166th edition of the great race?
 Will it be one of Joseph O'Brien's five horses from Ireland, or Ciaron Maher's team of largely imports?
 Could Shockletz win, 17 years after his sire Shocking got the job done?
 Could Jamie Melham make it two in a row on Future History , or could her husband Ben earn bragging rights with victory on Zahrann ? That's not even touching the sides of the potential stories. I can't wait!
 Regardless, we're in for a big contest, and we all hope the 23 horses make it home safe and sound.
 Good luck to everyone, and it's all ready to go!    
 React React Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:55pm Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:55pm The last runs for all 24 Melbourne Cup horses
 A By Andrew McGarry
 Point of Law's Geelong Cup victory makes him only one of three horses in today's Cup coming off a last-start win (Getty Images/Racing Photos) One of the guides to the Melbourne Cup each year is recent form, in particular the last run before the Cup for each horse in the race.
 Let's look at the Melbourne Cup dating back to 2009, when Shocking was the last horse to run on Derby Day — a first-place result in the Hotham Handicap over 2,500m — and go on to win the Cup.
 In the 17 Cups from 2009 to 2025, 12 of the winners had placed (come first, second or third) in their previous race before the Melbourne Cup.
 Six horses — Shocking, Americain (2010), Dunaden (2011), Almandin (2016),   Without A Fight (2023) and Half Yours (2025)— won their last race before winning the Cup.
 You don't have to have a top-three finish before the Cup to win the whole thing. Five have done this, the most recent was 2024 winner Knight's Choice , who backed up at Flemington after a fifth in the Bendigo Cup (G3, 2400m).
 So how does the field compare this year?
 Last start wins (3): Juja Kibo , So You Are , Point of Law .
 Last-start seconds (3): Sons And Lovers , Hopewell Rock , Shockletz .
 Last-start thirds (2): Enfjaar , Mr Monaco .
 Last start outside top three (15): Trustyourinstinct (4th), Knight's Choice (14th), Middle Earth (8th), Vauban (9th), Royal Supremacy (15th), Wine Dark Sea (11th), Asterix (12th), Goodie Two Shoes (10th), Onesmoothoperator (11th), Soul of Spain (8th), Zahrann (6th), Future History (9th), James J Braddock (6th), Kizlyar (11th), Strictly Business (16th), Zakouma (11th).
 React React Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:50pm Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:50pm Melbourne Cup horses 21-24
 A By Andrew McGarry
 21 - Strictly Business: Four-year-old mare trained by Thomas Carberry. Hasn't won a race since last year's Victoria Oaks over 2,500m. Recent runs poor, capped by last place in the Moonee Valley Cup 10 days ago. Hard to make a case. Dean Yendall rides.
 22 - Mr Monaco: Another Ciaron Maher-import, he won the Bart Cummings (2,500m) in April. Third in the Moonee Valley Cup, but was only 11th in the Sydney Cup over 3,200m this year. Apprentice Jabez Johnstone on board. Lightweight chance.
 23 - Zakouma: Six-year-old gelding, trained by Graham Begg. Won the Andrew Ramsden (2,800m) at Flemington in May. Aimed for this race, building up the kilometres in his legs. Ridden by WA gun William Pike. Needs to peak on Cup Day.
 24: Shockletz: Bottom-weight, five-year-old mare who won the Archer Stakes two months ago to make the field. Ciaron Maher-trained, she has had two solid runs since. Has 51kg, which her sire Shocking won the Cup with in 2009. Harry Coffey rides.
 React React Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:46pm Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:46pm Melbourne Cup horses 17-20
 A By Andrew McGarry
 17 - Future History: Veteran stayer, now trained by Greg Hickman, who made the field after horses withdrew. Last year's winner Jamie Melham gets the ride. Fifteenth in the Cup in 2023 in his only run over 3,200m. Looks faced with a big task.
 18 - James J Braddock: Northern hemisphere three-year-old trained by Joseph O'Brien, this gelding came third in the English Derby. A couple of ok runs over 2,400m followed. Drew the car park in barrier 24. Has Craig Williams on board, which is a plus.
 19 - Kizlyar: Another Joseph O'Brien entry, made the field when stablemate Defiantly was withdrawn by stewards. Can stay, winning over 4,000m in England, came second over 2,816m in August. Poor at Moonee Valley 10 days ago. Beau Mertens rides.
 20 - Point of Law: Ciaron Maher-import, intriguing but questions to answer. Ran first-up in Australia with a strong win in the Geelong Cup. Another NH three-year-old with good weight and barrier. But yet to run beyond 2,847m, and only its sixth start.
 React React Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:42pm Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:42pm Melbourne Cup horses 13-16
 A By Andrew McGarry
 13 - Onesmoothoperator: Former English international, now trained by Tim Fitzimmons. Won the Geelong Cup in 2024, and the Moonee Valley Cup last year. Failed to make the top 10 in both Cups. Not in as good form in 2026. Declan Bates on board.
 14 - Soul of Spain:   Chris Waller's other entry. Can run 3,200m (second in the Sydney Cup). Gets the most successful barrier in Cup history (five). A bit of rain would help a bit. A lot of rain would help a lot. Eighth in the Caulfield Cup. Needs to lift.
 15 - Zahrann: Irish horse, now trained by Ciaron Maher. Doesn't like it too wet, as in this year's Turnbull Stakes. Has been good but not spectacular over 2,000 and 2,400m. Fourth in the Caulfield Cup, in the mix here. Ridden by Ben Melham.
 16 - So You Are: Got in the Cup after winning the Bendigo Cup,   like Knight's Choice who came fifth in 2024. No turn of foot, but a dour stayer who should get 3,200m. In form, has Rachel King on board. Rise in class here, but a chance for trainer Bjorn Baker.
 React React Key Event
 Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:39pm Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:39pm Melbourne Cup horses 9-12
 M By Michael Doyle
 9- Asterix : A nice winter in Queensland where the eight-year-old gelding won the   Group 3 Tattersall’s Cup (2,400m) meant there were high hopes for the Melbourne spring. Trained by   Chris Waller, he was caught up in the nasty Caulfield Cup fall which hampered his run. His CV does not suggest he'll be in the placings, but jockey   Jye McNeil is a Melbourne Cup winner (Twighlight Payment, 2020).
 10 -   Goodie Two Shoes :   Joseph O’Brien-trained Goodie Two Shoes was second in last year's Cup, and is a genuine stayer with wins over 3,200m. Like last year,   Wayne Lordan will be on his back as he tries to go one better. Wasn't fancied last year, and is not a hot tip this year either. But his CV suggests he can give this Cup a real crack.
 11 -   Juja Kibo : There is a lot to like about this five-year-old gelding. A winner in his last two starts, Group 2 Moonee Valley Gold Cup (2,500m) and Group 2 The   Metropolitan (2,400), Juja Kibo is a strong contender for trainer Ciaron Maher.   Sam Clipperton has the ride, and the 55kg weight makes him a real contender.
 12 -   Hopewell Rock : Many like the look of this four-year-old gelding. With just 10 races under his belt, he has won over 2,816, so the distance won't be an issue. Young British trainer George Boughey is hoping to make his mark on the Cup, and he as plenty of credentials; training   Via Sistina before she moved to Australia. Jockey   Zac Lloyd has had a terrific 2026 and would like to cap off the year with a maiden Melbourne Cup win.
 React React Key Event
 Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:33pm Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:33pm Melbourne Cup horses 5-8
 M By Michael Doyle
 5 - Vauban : A fan-favourite at Flemington, the eight-year-old gelding is back for his fourth Melbourne Cup. This is his second Cup trained by   Gai Waterhouse and Adrian Bott, who helped him to a Melbourne Cup best sixth last year. He was ninth last start at the Geelong Cup and has   Jordan Childs on his back. It's hard to see him finally getting up for a win, but it would be terrific.  
 6 - Enfjaar : British trainer   Roger Varian brings Enfjaar, a six-year-old gelding that impressed with a third place finish in the Caulfield Cup. Prior to that, it won the Group 3   Glorious Stakes at Goodwood over 2,414m. That win at Goodwood is furthest he's run for victory, so the 3,200m may be a challenge. He will be ridden by Irish jockey   Ray Dawson.
 7 -   Royal Supremacy : Another horse for trainer   Ciaron Maher, this five-year-old gelding was 15th in last year's Cup. He was also 15th in last month's Caulfield Cup, but does have a recent win in the Group 3   Jra Cup over 2,000m in September. A group 1 winner in The   Metropolitan, he will be ridden by   Ben Allen and could be an outside shot at a placing.
 8 -   Wine Dark Sea : Lightly run, this four-year-old was disappointing in the Caulfield Cup where he faded to 11th. He has won at   2,715m in Britan's   Group 3 Geoffrey Freer Stakes earlier this year. Trained by   Harry Charlton and ridden by Damien Lane, his rough outing at Caulfield and a wide barrier (23) makes it hard to see a great result.
 React React Key Event
 Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:30pm Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:30pm Melbourne Cup horses 1-4
 M By Michael Doyle
 1 - Sons and Lovers : A five-year-old gelding is one of five horses in the Cup trained by Ireland's Joseph O'Brien. He is the top weight carrying 57.5kg, but that should not bother this international stayer. A winner at 3,000m means the Melbourne Cup distance will be no problem, he has won the Group 2 Red Sea Turf in Saudi Arabia and the Group 2 Prix Maurice de Nieuil in France this year. He will be ridden by 2025 Irish Jockey Champion   Dylan Browne McMonagle.
 2 - Trustyourinstinct : Arguably the most fancied of the five Joseph O'Brien-trained contenders, this six-year-old gelding is a genuine stayer. His last run was in a fourth-place finish in Septmeber's Group 1 Irish St. Leger, and before that won the Group 2 Curragh Cup in Ireland. A serious horse with genuine winning chances, ridden by champion jockey   James McDonald.
 3 - Knight's Choice : The 2024 Cup winner lines up for another crack at the great race. Trainer   Sheila Laxon has put two horses in the Melbourne Cup, and both won the race: Knight's Choice 2024,   Ethereal 2001. Knight's Choice is the only former winning in the field. and will be carrying 56.5kg. Just like two years ago, Robbie Dolan will be in the saddle. Probably not fancied, but wasn't in 2024 either.
 4 - Middle Earth : The first of seven horses trained by   Ciaron Maher, Middle Earth will be ridden by duel Melbourne Cup winner Mark Zahra. Ninth in the Caulfield Cup and eighth in the Cox Plate is not the best form leading in, but should have no problems over 3,200m.

 Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:26pm Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:26pm Robbie Williams shines at Flemington
 M By Michael Doyle
 One of the most popular artists on our shores, Britain's Robbie Williams, is performing at Flemington.
 (Getty) He is putting on quite a show, and the huge crowd is lapping it up.
 He opens with Feel, before moving into his hit, Rock DJ.
 Then the big one, Angels.
 I think everyone at Flemington is screaming this belter out.
 AND NOW he breaks out into Let Me Entertain You. Oh, the crowd is loving this.
 I am loving this.
 Loading Twitter content React React Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:25pm Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:25pm How often do favourites win the Melbourne Cup?
 A By Andrew McGarry
 A decent amount of favourites have won the Melbourne Cup - but the last one to salute was Fiorente in 2013 (Getty Images) As you might imagine in a race with 24 (or even 23) runners, there are a lot of factors in a Melbourne Cup, including the barriers, the track surface, who can get cover (not get caught wide), the tempo of the race and the runs that different horses get (or don't get).
 Back in 2014, my friend and colleague Daniel Franklin , who puts together the marvellous interactive Cup Guide every year for ABC, did an interesting fact-check story before the 2014 Melbourne Cup, which was won by Protectionist.
 Checking the exhaustive stats, he found that to that point, 34 favourites had won out of 153 Melbourne Cups, or a tick over 22.2 per cent (a Richie Benaud stat, there).
 Since that point, however, it's been a bad run for favourites. Fiorente, in 2013, was the last Melbourne Cup favourite to finish first.
 Before the 2014 Cup, 70 of the 153 Melbourne Cup favourites had run at least a place (come first, second or third). That's equal to 46 per cent of the time.
 But again, the intervening 12 years have not been kind to the horses on top of the betting. Only three of the last 12 favourites (Hartnell in 2016, Tiger Moth in 2021 and Incentivise in 2022) have finished in the top three. That means the total equals 73 favourites out of 165 races have run a place — or 44.2 per cent.
 An explanation? With the internationalisation of the Cup, we have a lot more horses coming from overseas, plenty still rejecting a pre-Cup run Down Under.
 This means that favouritism often is led by rumours out of the quarantine centre at Werribee, where the internationals do their trackwork after landing in Australia.
 That's racing, but it does make it harder and harder to line up form between horses from various countries around the world and those that have run here and are used to conditions.
 React React Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:20pm Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:20pm Melbourne Cup by the numbers: the barriers
 A By Andrew McGarry
 Looking at history, here are the most successful barriers for winners (in descending order), with the horse running from these barriers this year.
 Ten wins: Barrier 5 (Soul of Spain)
 Nine wins: Barrier 11 (Zahrann)
 Seven wins: Barrier 8 (Enfjaar)
 Six wins: Barrier 4 (Strictly Business)
 Five wins: 3 (Sons And Lovers), 10 (Zakouma), 13 (Onesmoothoperator), 21 (Royal Supremacy)
 Least successful barriers
 Zero wins* — Barrier 18 (Trustyourinstinct)
 One win — Barrier 15 (Hopewell Rock)
 Two wins — Barriers 7 (So You Are) and 9 (Point of Law)
 * Verry Elleegant drew barrier 19 in 2022, but after a scratching it started from barrier 18. No horse that has drawn 18 has won the Cup.
 React React Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:19pm Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:19pm How to follow the Melbourne Cup
 M By Michael Doyle
 How do I watch the melbourne cup live
 - Michael 
 G'day Michael.
 The Nine Network has the television rights to broadcast the 2026 Melbourne Cup.
 All 10 races at Flemington will be broadcast on Channel Nine , and streamed on Nine Now .
 ABC Sport will have live digital coverage of Melbourne Cup Day with a live blog. You can also listen to the live call of the Melbourne Cup on the radio, online, or via the ABC Listen app.
 React React Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:15pm Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:15pm Melbourne Cup by the numbers: The saddlecloths
 A By Andrew McGarry
 Horses in the Melbourne Cup are numbered in descending order of weight carried, so the topweight carries number one on the saddlecloth, the lightest carries number 24, and so on.
 Here are the most successful numbers (saddlecloths) in the Melbourne Cup:
 Number 4 —12 wins (This year Middle Earth )
 Number 1 — 11 wins* (This year Sons And Lovers )
 Number 12 — 11 wins (This year Hopewell Rock )
 Number 8 — 9 wins (This year Wine Dark Sea )
 Number 11 — 8 wins (This year   Juja Kibo )
 * Sons And Lovers as the topweight has recent history against it. When Gold Trip won in 2022, it was just the third win by the topweight in the past 69 years.
 React React Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:10pm Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:10pm Melbourne Cup storylines: The jockeys
 A By Andrew McGarry
 James McDonald won the big race on Derby Day on Stormy Macro - can he double up with the Melbourne Cup on Trustyourinstinct? (Getty Images/Racing Photos) It's fair to say that no jockey comes into today's Melbourne Cup in better form than James McDonald .
 The New Zealand jockey — otherwise known as J-Mac — tuned up for the race that stops a nation with no less than four winners on Derby Day, including Stormy Marco in the Victoria Derby (G1, 2,500m) and star mare Lady Shenandoah in the Empire Rose Stakes (G1, 1,600m). He rides Trustyourinstinct for Joseph O'Brien, and a win would give him his second Cup.
 There are a number of other jockeys who are looking for their second Cup victory.
 These include Craig Williams , who won on Vow and Declare in 2019 and is on board James J Braddock; and Robbie Dolan , the all-singing, all-riding Irishman can make it two if Knight's Choice follows up Dolan's win on … Knight's Choice two years ago.
 There's also Jamie Melham , who won last year on Half Yours. She can make it two on Future History .
 Jamie Melham's husband Ben Melham is again a rival, as he tries to earn his first Cup aboard Zahrann. 
 Of course, Mark Zahra can trump them all with a third, if he wins on Middle Earth to add to his wins in 2022 and 2023 (Gold Trip and Without A Fight).
 Aside from Ben Melham there are 17 other jockeys hoping to add their names to the Melbourne Cup honour roll for the first time.
 If Sons And Lovers ( Dylan Brown McMonagle ), Enfjaar ( Ray Dawson ), or Goodie Two Shoes ( Wayne Lordan ) win, then whichever jockey wins will be the first international jockey since Ryan Moore on Protectionist in 2014 to win the Cup.
 If So You Are wins, then Rachel King will become the third woman to ride a Cup winner after Michelle Payne (2015) and Jamie Melham last year.
 If Mr Monaco salutes, then Jabez Johnstone will not only join the honour roll, he will become the first apprentice to win the Cup since 16-year-old Ray Neville on Rimfire back in 1948.
 The other prospective first-timers are Jordan Childs (Vauban), Ben Allen (Royal Supremacy), Damian Lane (Wine Dark Sea), Sam Clipperton (Juja Kibo), Zac Lloyd (Hopewell Rock), Declan Bates (Onesmoothoperator), Tommy Berry (Soul of Spain), Beau Mertens (Kizlyar), Ethan Brown (Point of Law), Michael Dee (Strictly Business), William Pike (Zakouma) and Harry Coffey (Shockletz).
 React React Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:04pm Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 2:04pm Can an Australian-bred horse win the Melbourne Cup again?
 A By Andrew McGarry
 Trainer Sheila Laxon won the Cup in 2024 with the Australian-bred Knight's Choice - can they do it again? (Getty Images) It's been an interesting time for the Melbourne Cup — or maybe things go in cycles.
 Even five years ago, pretty much everyone agreed that Australian-bred stayers were such a low priority in local racing that many of the big trainers had decided to look overseas for their challengers for the Cup.
 The whole tone of the race was changing, and yet — not quite.
 Two years ago, 100-1 outsider Knight's Choice , trained by Sheila Laxon and John Symons,   struck a blow for local breeding when he won the Cup in a tight finish.
 Was it an outlier? No, it turned out, as Half Yours went on from his Caulfield Cup win to take out the big one at Flemington as well.
 So, can Australia make it three on the trot, so to speak?
 Well, there's a non-zero chance. There are four locally-bred entries - Knight's Choice, So You Are , Strictly Business and Zakouma .
 Knight's Choice is back for a tilt at a second Cup; So You Are has won four races in a row, capped by the Bendigo Cup victory that got him into the Cup; Strictly Business is a mare whose last win was in the 2025 Victoria Oaks at Flemington; and Zakouma has been given the Bart Cummings treatment by trainer Grahame Begg, flying under the radar in a 10,000m-raced prep.
 Below is the list of the seven Australian-bred Cup winners since the internationalisation of the race in 1993. We'll find out in a few hours whether that number can increase to eight or not:

 Loading Twitter content React React Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 1:43pm Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 1:43pm Melbourne Cup storylines: The trainers
 A By Andrew McGarry
 Trainer Ciaron Maher has seven chances to win this year's Melbourne Cup (Getty Images) There are five chances to add to Ireland's four wins in the race — and they're all for the same man.
 Joseph O'Brien could become the youngest trainer (at 33) to win a third Melbourne Cup with Sons And Lovers, Trustyourinstinct, Goodie Two Shoes, James J Braddock or Kizlyar.
 If he breaks the record, O'Brien would take the place of French trainer Etienne de Mestre , who won five Cups in the 1800s, with his third in 1867 with Tim Whiffler at the age of 35.
 There are a number of trainers who could add to England's sole win in the Cup (Charlie Appleby with Cross Counter in 2018).
 Roger Varian has Enfjaar, Harry Charlton has Wine Dark Sea, and George Boughey has Hopewell Rock.
 Between O'Brien and Ciaron Maher , the pair literally have half the field.
 Added to O'Brien's five entries are Maher's septet — Middle Earth, Royal Supremacy, Juja Kibo, Zahrann, Point of Law, Mr Monaco and Shockletz. If any of these come home, it would be Maher's second win after Gold Trip in 2022.
 Maher is a leading proponent of the Aussie "imports" strategy for the Cup. Of his seven horses, only Shockletz (NZ-bred) is vaguely local, while the rest are from Britain or Ireland.
 Chris Waller no longer has Asterix, but he does have Irish-bred Soul of Spain in the running. If it runs first, Waller would have a second Cup win to add to Verry Elleegant in 2021.
 Gai Waterhouse could also add a second victory if (French-bred) Vauban gets up (and a first for co-trainer Adrian Bott ). A win would see Waterhouse join Sheila Laxon (Ethereal, Knight's Choice) as the only female trainers to win two Melbourne Cups.
 Laxon is going for a third Melbourne Cup — with the same horse as her second as Knight's Choice goes for a second win in three years. Her co-trainer John Symons would win his second.
 Then there are the trainers looking to break through and add their names to the honour roll for the first time (aside from those already mentioned).
 These are Bjorn Baker with So You Are, Tim Fitzimmons with Onesmoothoperator, Gregory Hickman with Future History, Thomas Carberry with Strictly Business and Grahame Begg with Zakouma.

 A By Andrew McGarry
 Enfjaar (L) finished a close third behind Kingswood and Saint George in the Caulfield Cup - can the English horse take home the Melbourne Cup? (Getty Images) While several international horses have been withdrawn from the race in the lead-up to the field being finalised, there are still plenty of "raiders" willing to try their luck to take the Melbourne Cup overseas.
 Last year, Joseph O'Brien-trained   Goodie Two Shoes fell one place short of taking the Melbourne Cup back to Ireland, losing to Half Yours by a couple of lengths.
 This time round, a third of the field are internationally trained, not to mention the Aussie "imports".
 And where are these horses coming from? Ireland and England.
 The first two modern "raiders" who came to Australia for the sole purpose of winning the Melbourne Cup were Vintage Crop and Drum Taps in 1993. Their campaign — and Vintage Crop's win for Irish trainer Dermot Weld — was seen as the start of the internationalisation of the Cup.
 There are a few horses trying to do what Vintage Crop did and win without a lead-up race in Australia.
 Aside from Goodie Two Shoes, whose last run this time round was 10th in the Kilternan Stakes (G3, 2,414m) at Leopardstown, trainer   Joseph O'Brien has Sons And Lovers, who came second in the Kilternan Stakes; Trustyourinstinct , who came fourth in the Irish St Leger at the Curragh (G1, 2,816m); James J Braddock , who came sixth in the Kilternan Stakes.
 O'Brien also has Kizlyar , who had to race in Australia to make the field. He came 11th in the Moonee Valley Cup (G2, 2,500m), but still got in after withdrawals.
 The other true raider — here just for this race — is Hopewell Rock , trained by Englishman George Boughey . Hopewell Rock last ran second in the Ebor Handicap (G2, 2,786m), England's biggest handicap race.
 English trainer Roger Varian has brought over Enfjaar , who produced a nice run to come third in the Caulfield Cup two-and-a-half weeks ago (G1, 2,400m). Varian's compatriot Harry Charlton trains Wine Dark Sea , who also ran in the Caulfield Cup, finishing 11th.

 Loading Twitter content React React Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 1:07pm Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 1:07pm How does the track rating system work?
 A By Andrew McGarry
 If you're new to racing, or if you only tune in once a year on a day like today, the description of the track rating may confuse you.
 The system uses different ratings on a scale from 1 to 10.
 Rating 1 is a dry, hard track and 2 a firm track. Ratings 3 and 4 are "Good", with 3 a better covering of grass and 4 a track with some give in it.
 For everyday races, track managers aim to have the surface at a Good 3 or 4.
 Ratings 5 to 7 are Soft, meaning that there is more moisture and give in the track. By the time you get to a 7, it's a more rain-affected track that will start to chop up during the course of the meeting.
 Right now, we are at a Soft 5, which means there is some moisture in the track but it's not deteriorating yet. In fact, the lack of recent rain means we could see an upgrade to a Good 4 at some stage.
 The last three ratings, 8 to 10, are Heavy.
 That would come after a lot of rain and increasing of deterioration in the track.
 When it gets to a Heavy track, only so-called "mudlarks" will cope with it. Organisers will be hoping we don't get to that stage today.

 Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 12:31pm Tue 3 Nov 2026 at 12:31pm Stewards inquiry as Melbourne Cup contender scratched
 M By Michael Doyle
 — reporting by AAP 
 High-profile trainer Chris Waller has been questioned by stewards after his Melbourne Cup contender Asterix was found to have had the medication Penetrene administered to both forelegs in its stable just hours before Australia's greatest race.
 Asterix, part-owned by former New Zealand international cricketer Mark Greatbatch, was scratched from today's $10 million Flemington showpiece.
 Loading Twitter content Penetrene is generally allowed to be used on horses, except on race days.
 "Penetrene is a topical product marketed as an anti-inflammatory and analgesic liniment," Racing Victoria said in a statement.
 "Penetrene is used topically on horses for symptomatic relief of muscle strains, sprains and muscle soreness.
 "Any substance administered to a horse on raceday, including any topical application amongst any other route of administration is considered a medication."
 Stewards will continue their inquiries into the circumstances with Waller later on Tuesday.
 Asterix's scratching leaves Waller with only one contender - $21 fancy Soul Of Spain - in the Cup. Asterix had been a $51 chance.
 It also leaves 2020 Cup-winning jockey Jye McNeil without a ride in Flemington's $10 million showpiece.
 McNeil rebounded from the news to finish second with Royal Press in the opening race on the card, behind Damian Lane on Amelia's Affair.
 Meanwhile, popular jockey Harry Coffey has arrived at Flemington to ride Shockletz in the Cup, just two days after having a plate inserted to repair his fractured collarbone.
 Coffey required surgery after his scary Victoria Derby day fall, but was all smiles as he flapped his 'wing' at punters when he walked towards the mounting yard.
 Rival jockeys lauded Coffey's bravery after he was declared fit by Racing Victoria's chief medical officer Dr Ben Barresi.
 "They always say jockeys are made of different stuff and he's proving that," said Rachel King, who will partner So You Are in the Cup.
 "It just proves how much it means to us jockeys ... Melbourne Cup day is the biggest day of the year."
 Superstar jockey James McDonald, who will ride Trustyourinstinct for Irish trainer O'Brien and billionaire owner-breeder JP McManus, rates Shockletz among the main challengers.
 "(Coffey) is tougher than most of us," McDonald said.
 "It's like a grand final for us jockeys and trainers. This is the race that stops the nation, so we'd get up for anything."
